summary: The root W-H-Y primarily signifies a swift, secret, and subtle communication or indication.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.gloss: revealed to him; spake; made known, to him by revelation

parts.t: made known, to him by revelation

headwords.def: أَوْحَى إِلَيْهِ He (God) revealed to him; or spake, or made known, to him by revelation Also, He suggested to him; or put into his mind. (Mughnee voce أَنْ .)

parts.t: (S, Mgh, Msb, K; applied in this sense to death. (S, Mgh, Msb.)

headwords.def: وَحِىٌّ Hasty; (K;) quick; (S, Mgh, Msb, K; applied in this sense to death. (S, Mgh, Msb.)

headwords.gloss: haste; haste to be first; before
headwords.def: الوَحَآءَ الوَحَآءَ [Make thou] haste; or haste to be first, or before, or beforehand: haste; &c. (S, TA.)

parts.t: see an ex. in the first paragraph of art.

headwords.def: فِى أَوْحَى مُدَّةٍ In the shortest period: see an ex. in the first paragraph of art. ثقف .

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
